23: ## Overview
24: 
25: **Scope:** original English base game, main rulebook **v1.2**, base glossary, official base FAQ and official base Icon Overview. Marine Worlds and optional solo mode are excluded.
26: 
27: In Ark Nova you plan and build a modern, scientifically managed zoo. You build enclosures according to the animals' way of life and support conservation projects to ensure the preservation of animal species. Gathering diverse animals increases the attractiveness of your zoo, advancing you on the **Appeal track** and generating higher revenues; careful stewardship lets you support conservation projects, advancing you on the **Conservation track** with corresponding bonuses. These two tracks progress in **opposite directions**. If your counters meet or cross at the end of your own turn or during a break, final turns begin. Whoever achieves the best combination of appeal and conservation has built the most successful zoo and wins.
28: 
29: Association work in different zoo associations allows you to partner with zoos and universities around the world; together with specialists and sponsors, they help you manage the tasks needed to achieve your goals.
30: 
31: Ark Nova does not play in formal rounds: players simply take turns (clockwise), one turn at a time, until the end of the game is triggered. In between there are **breaks** — administration phases in which you discard down to your hand limit, recall workers, and gain income. On your turn you always perform one action using one of the 5 Action cards displayed below your zoo map; the position (card slot) of the Action card determines how much you can do with that action.

60: ## Setup
61: 
62: **Global setup**
63: 1. Place the game board in the center. Place the **Break token** on the start space of the Break track corresponding to your player count (e.g., with three players, the space marked 3).
64: 2. Shuffle the 9 **Bonus tiles** and place a random tile **face up** on each of the **4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8 conservation**. Do not place tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons. Return the remaining 5 tiles to the box (unused).
65: 3. Shuffle the **Zoo cards** into a face-down deck on its board space. Deal 6 face-down cards to the display spaces on the board.
66: 4. Place the 2 organizers next to the board as the general supply.
67: 5. Place the **Association board** next to the game board, leaving room for one row of cards above and one row below.
68:    - 5a. Place 1 partner zoo of each continent and 1 university of each kind on the spaces provided on the Association board.
69:    - 5b. Shuffle the **Base Conservation Project cards** and keep them face down next to the board. In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up below the board; otherwise the 3 topmost.
70:    - 5c. **2-player game only:** take 6 player tokens of an unused color and cover: on the face-up Base Conservation Project cards, the left level on the left card, the middle level on the middle card, and the right level on the right card; and on the Association board, the three spaces in the left column of the donation area. Covered levels/spaces are blocked and cannot be used by either player. **With three or four players, none of these project levels or donation spaces is blocked at setup.**
71: 6. Shuffle the **Final Scoring cards** and place them face down next to the Association board.
72: 7. Randomly determine a start player. Turn order is clockwise.
73: 
74: **Personal setup (each player)**
75: - **A.** Take a random Map A zoo map and place it that side up (recommended for the first game; all Map A copies are identical). Map 0 suits beginners after the first game. Maps 1–8 (reverse sides) are advanced maps, each with an individual special ability: with these, take 2 random zoo maps and choose 1 of the advanced maps — or lay out player count +1 advanced maps and choose 1 each in reverse order of play. Return unselected maps to the box. Map A's ability (same for all players): at the beginning of the game, place an empty 3-space enclosure **and a kiosk** on the indicated spaces. The printed kiosk already counts as built; place a kiosk tile over it as a reminder. You may build adjacent to it.
76: - **B.** Take one set of Action cards (Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors). Place one card **side I up** under each of the five card slots on your zoo map: the **Animals** card under the leftmost slot (showing 1), the remaining 4 randomly under the other slots.
77: - **C.** Choose a color and take all its components.
78:   - **C1.** Place your appeal, conservation, and reputation counters on the first spaces of their tracks. On the **Appeal track**, stagger by turn order: start player on space 0, second player on space 1, third on space 2, fourth on space 3.
79:   - **C2.** Place 7 player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; keep the rest next to your map for later use.
80:   - **C3.** Place 1 association worker on the notepad of your zoo map (the active worker) and the remaining 3 lying down on the designated spaces below the notepad.
81: - **D.** Take 25 money and put it on your notepad.
82: - **E.** Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and place them next to your zoo map. You may look at them at any time, but keep them hidden from other players.
83: - **F.** Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 as hand cards and discard the other 4 to a face-up discard pile on the board. Keep hand cards hidden. (Tip from the rulebook: choose 1–2 Sponsor and 2–3 Animal cards without conditions you cannot fulfill early, ideally matching the Base Conservation Projects on display.)
84: - **G.** After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

The first four are received immediately when uncovered and again as break income; the last three are one-time. Take a chosen bonus before or after its project's reward. 98: **Your zoo map:** buildings go in the large central area. You may not build on rock and water spaces (some animals need an enclosure next to rock or water). A built-on space is "covered." Spaces with a special icon may not be built on until you upgrade your Build Action card. Some spaces show a **placement bonus**, gained immediately when you cover them. 100: ## Turn Structure
101: 
102: **Taking a turn.** You may not do nothing: playing zero animals or building zero buildings is not a legal action. Use the alternative X-token action when you cannot or do not want to execute a regular action.
103: 
104:  On your turn, choose one of your 5 Action cards, shift it lower than the others to show it is in use, and perform its action with the strength of its card slot (1 = far left through 5 = far right; the further right, the more powerful). After completing the action, remove the card from its slot, shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1.
105: 
106: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.
107: 
108: **"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.
109: 
110: **Upgrading Action cards.** All Action cards start on side I. When you receive a card upgrade, flip one Action card of your choice from side I to side II (it stays in its slot); its improved action is available **from your next action**, while it immediately counts as upgraded for conditions. The current action keeps the strength and kind set at its start; an upgrade gained during it does not add side-II capabilities to it. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. One of them allows you to choose an alternative — so you cannot upgrade all of your Action cards.
111: 
112: **The Break track.** At the start of the game and after each break, the Break token sits on the starting space for your player count. Various actions and card effects advance it toward the end of the track. When it reaches the **last space**, you call a break for everyone: the break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get **1 X-token** for reaching the last space. Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. After the break, the token returns to its starting space.
113: 
114: **Break procedure** (all players, in order):
115: 1. **Hand card limit — 3 cards normally, or 5 with the hand-limit university:** discard cards of your choice down to that limit.
116: 2. **Tokens on Action cards:** return any Multiplier, Venom, and/or Constriction tokens on your Action cards to the supply; they no longer have any effect.
117: 3. **Association board:** return all your association workers to your notepad (active again — all tasks are again available at 1 worker). **Restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent and each university kind**, except kinds **already owned by every player**; do not add duplicate available tiles.
118: 4. **Replenish display:** discard the two bottom cards of the display (folders 1 and 2), move the remaining cards down, and refill the display.
119: 5. **Take income** (when multiple players take display cards, **refill the display after each player**; usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, begin with the player who initiated the break — or the affected player closest to them — and proceed clockwise):
120:    - a. Money according to your zoo's **appeal** (the amount printed next to your counter on the Appeal track; e.g., space 7 pays 11 money).
121:    - b. **Kiosk income:** for each kiosk, take 1 money per unique building, special enclosure, **occupied** standard enclosure, and pavilion adjacent to it (sharing at least one side of a space). An empty standard enclosure provides no income, but an empty special enclosure does.
122:    - c. All income marked with the break-income icon on your Sponsor cards and on your **activated** zoo-map bonuses (those uncovered by supporting conservation projects).
123:    **When more than one player receives a display card during break income, resolve those players clockwise starting with the break initiator (or the first affected player clockwise from them). Refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.** This ordering and the between-player refill apply together.
124: 6. **Break track:** return the Break token to the starting space for your player count. Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

142: ## Actions
143: 
144: The position of the Action card sets its strength; each card has a stronger side II once upgraded.
145: 
146: ### CARDS action
147: - **Side I:** Advance the Break token **2 spaces** (you do not gain money for this). Then either **draw from the deck** — compare the strength of the slot with the table on the card and draw the indicated number of cards (maximum 3), after which you might have to discard a card from your hand (one just drawn or one already held) — or **snap**: with strength **5 or more**, instead take exactly **1 card of your choice from the display** into your hand, regardless of your reputation. Replenish the display at the end of your turn. There is no in-turn hand limit; you only discard to your limit during breaks.
148: - **Side II:** Advance the Break token 2 spaces, then draw cards from the deck **and/or from within reputation range** (the display up to your Reputation counter), in any order, using the upgraded table on the card (e.g., at strength 5 you take 4 cards and discard 1). The display is not replenished until your turn is complete. Snapping now works from strength **3** (strength above 3 makes no difference to a snap). **On either side, snapping takes exactly one display card of any reputation, with no deck draw; the reputation restriction applies only to the side-II draw option, not snapping.** Upgrading the Cards action also lets you progress **past 9 reputation** on the Reputation track.

"Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. 269: ### SPONSORS action
270: - **Side I:** Play **exactly 1 Sponsor card** from your hand: the action's strength must be at least the card's **level**, and you must meet any conditions on the card's left side. Execute its instant effect and/or its recurring effect (if triggered by the card's own icon), then place it next to your zoo map. **OR:** advance the Break token a number of steps equal to the strength and take that much money — you take the full money even if the Break token doesn't need all the steps to reach the final space.
271: - **Side II:** Play **one or more** Sponsor cards:
272:   - **Level budget:** action strength **+1** must be at least the sum of all played cards' levels. X-tokens may push strength beyond 5.
273:   - **Card sources:** use your hand and/or the display within reputation range. Pay each display card's folder number as an additional cost; replenish only at turn end. Sponsors II also permits cards whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.
274:   - **Effect order:** play the cards one after another. Fully execute each card's instant effects before the next; defer its "after finishing" effects until the action is finished.
275:   - **Money option:** if you instead advance the Break token, take the money **twice**.
276: 
277: **Sponsor card layout:** level in the upper-left corner (with any build-adjacency water/rock requirement beside it); play conditions on the left; the card's own icon in the upper-right corner. A recurring effect appears at the top on a blue background — purple if it is income in every break. A one-off play effect has a yellow background (lower-left); a final-scoring effect has a brown background (lower-right), with a vertical brown strip behind the level as a reminder once cards are overlapped. If a Sponsor card's effect refers to an icon on the card itself, it counts — but only icons in the upper-right corners of cards are used (plus the rock and water icons in the upper-left). Some Sponsor cards place **unique buildings** (from the 15 tiles) into your zoo, subject to any water/rock adjacency shown; a certain minimum reputation is required to play certain Sponsor cards.
278: 
279: ### X-TOKEN action (alternative action)
280: If you cannot or do not want to perform any of the 5 actions, take exactly **1 X-token** instead. You must still select an Action card, move it to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right; the slot's strength and the card's upgrade state are irrelevant. If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.
281: 
282: ## Scoring / Victory Conditions
283: 
284: **During the game.** Your appeal determines your money income each break. The Conservation track has 4 spaces with a one-time effect when you reach or pass them:
285: - **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.
286: - **5 and 8 conservation points:** take either 5 money or one of the Bonus tiles next to that space. Execute a chosen tile immediately, then remove it from the game. The 5-money option remains even after both Bonus tiles there are gone.
287: - **10 conservation points:** the first time any player reaches or exceeds 10, **all players** choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile). If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
288: 
289: **End of the game.**
290: - **When to check your zoo:** check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**.
291: - **End condition:** your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track.
292: - **Appeal received during another player's turn:** the **zoo owner who received that appeal** waits for the end of **their own turn**, or a break, to check their zoo for the end trigger. This is the receiving zoo owner's turn, rather than the other player's turn. Another player may trigger the end first.
293: - **Last turns:** the triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**. If the end is triggered during a break, **all players** take one more turn.
294: 
295: **Final scoring.**
296: 1. Score your Final Scoring card(s) and all your cards with the end-of-game icon. Each Final Scoring card can grant up to 4 additional conservation points (by table or text, counting your universities, the cards in front of you, and their icons); you can never gain more than **4 conservation points from a single Final Scoring card**.
297: 2. Compute Victory Points: look at the scoring area where your Conservation counter is located and find the **lowest Appeal value in that scoring area** — this is your **Target Number**. **Victory Points = your Appeal value − your Target Number.**
298: 3. The player with the highest positive Victory Point total wins. **Tiebreaker:** the tied player who supported the most conservation projects wins (count the player tokens removed from the left side of the zoo map). If still tied, the tied players share the victory.
299: 
300: Note from the rulebook: to have a positive score, your Appeal counter and Conservation counter have to cross one another.
301: 
302: ## Special Rules & Edge Cases
303: 
304: - **Reputation cap:** reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action; on space 15, further reputation converts to 1 appeal per step instead.
305: - **Interactive effects** on Animal cards apply to you only if your zoo has **5 or more appeal**.

34:  INTRODUCTION & GOAL OF THE GAME 
35: In Ark Nova you plan and build a modern, scientifically 
36: managed zoo. You build enclosures according to the 
37: animals’ way of life and support conservation projects to 
38: ensure the preservation of animal species.
39: Gathering diverse animals increases the attractiveness 
40: of your zoo, advancing you on the Appeal track and 
41: generating higher revenues. Likewise, careful stewardship 
42: of the animals allows you to support conservation projects, 
43: such as breeding programs, that lead to your advancement 
44: on the Conservation track and corresponding bonuses. 
45: These two tracks progress in opposite directions – if your 
46: counters meet, the game ends. Whoever achieves the best 
47: combination of appeal and conservation has built the most 
48: successful zoo and wins the game. 
49: Association work in different zoo associations allows you 
50: to partner with zoos and universities around the world. 
51: Together, with specialists and sponsors, they will help you 
52: manage the various tasks needed to achieve your goals.
53: Both the designer and the publisher have made every effort 
54: to be realistic in the implementation of this game. In rare 
55: cases, however, concessions have been made for the sake 
56: of the game mechanics. For example, the koala has the 
57: subclass bear, which is often used colloquially, but does not 
58: correspond to reality. The same applies to the enclosure 
59: requirements.

22: 
23: ## Overview
24: 
25: **Scope:** original English base game, main rulebook **v1.2**, base glossary, official base FAQ and official base Icon Overview. Marine Worlds and optional solo mode are excluded.
26: 
27: In Ark Nova you plan and build a modern, scientifically managed zoo. You build enclosures according to the animals' way of life and support conservation projects to ensure the preservation of animal species. Gathering diverse animals increases the attractiveness of your zoo, advancing you on the **Appeal track** and generating higher revenues; careful stewardship lets you support conservation projects, advancing you on the **Conservation track** with corresponding bonuses. These two tracks progress in **opposite directions**. If your counters meet or cross at the end of your own turn or during a break, final turns begin. Whoever achieves the best combination of appeal and conservation has built the most successful zoo and wins.
28: 
29: Association work in different zoo associations allows you to partner with zoos and universities around the world; together with specialists and sponsors, they help you manage the tasks needed to achieve your goals.
30: 
31: Ark Nova does not play in formal rounds: players simply take turns (clockwise), one turn at a time, until the end of the game is triggered. In between there are **breaks** — administration phases in which you discard down to your hand limit, recall workers, and gain income. On your turn you always perform one action using one of the 5 Action cards displayed below your zoo map; the position (card slot) of the Action card determines how much you can do with that action.
32: 
33: ## Components
34: 
35: **Cards**
36: - 212 Zoo cards: 128 Animal cards, 64 Sponsor cards, 20 Conservation Project cards
37: - 12 Base Conservation Project cards
38: - 11 Final Scoring cards
39: - 20 double-sided Action cards (5 per set: Build, Cards, Animals, Association, Sponsors — each with side I and side II)
40: 
41: **Tiles & tokens**
42: - 90 standard enclosures in various sizes (1–5 spaces; both sides of a given size are the same shape — occupied side vs. empty side showing the size number)
43: - 12 special enclosures: 4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary
44: - 34 kiosk / pavilion tiles (kiosk and pavilion are opposite sides of the same tile)
45: - 20 partner zoos, 12 universities, 15 unique buildings
46: - 9 Bonus tiles
47: - 70 money tokens, 20 X-tokens
48: - 8 Venom tokens, 8 Constriction tokens, 8 Multiplier tokens
49: - 1 Break token
50: 
51: **Boards & mats**
52: - 1 game board (Zoo card deck and 6-card display, Reputation track, Appeal track, Conservation track, Break track, Bonus spaces)
53: - 1 Association board
54: - 8 player mats (zoo maps): 4× Map A (map for first-time players with a starting advantage — easy), 4× Map 0 (more bonus spaces — intermediate), and Maps 1–8 on the reverse sides (advanced, each with an individual special ability)
55: 
56: **Per player color** (black, blue, red, yellow): 3 counters (appeal, conservation, reputation), 25 player tokens, 4 association workers
57: 
58: **Other:** 2 organizers (general supply), 1 glossary, 1 icon overview, rulebook
59: 
60: ## Setup
61: 
62: **Global setup**
63: 1. Place the game board in the center. Place the **Break token** on the start space of the Break track corresponding to your player count (e.g., with three players, the space marked 3).
64: 2. Shuffle the 9 **Bonus tiles** and place a random tile **face up** on each of the **4 blank yellow spaces beside the Conservation track: two beside 5 conservation and two beside 8 conservation**. Do not place tiles on the two yellow spaces with icons. Return the remaining 5 tiles to the box (unused).
65: 3. Shuffle the **Zoo cards** into a face-down deck on its board space. Deal 6 face-down cards to the display spaces on the board.
66: 4. Place the 2 organizers next to the board as the general supply.
67: 5. Place the **Association board** next to the game board, leaving room for one row of cards above and one row below.

282: ## Scoring / Victory Conditions
283: 
284: **During the game.** Your appeal determines your money income each break. The Conservation track has 4 spaces with a one-time effect when you reach or pass them:
285: - **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.
286: - **5 and 8 conservation points:** take either 5 money or one of the Bonus tiles next to that space. Execute a chosen tile immediately, then remove it from the game. The 5-money option remains even after both Bonus tiles there are gone.
287: - **10 conservation points:** the first time any player reaches or exceeds 10, **all players** choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile). If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.
288: 
289: **End of the game.**
290: - **When to check your zoo:** check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**.
291: - **End condition:** your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track.
292: - **Appeal received during another player's turn:** the **zoo owner who received that appeal** waits for the end of **their own turn**, or a break, to check their zoo for the end trigger. This is the receiving zoo owner's turn, rather than the other player's turn. Another player may trigger the end first.
293: - **Last turns:** the triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**. If the end is triggered during a break, **all players** take one more turn.

295: **Final scoring.**
296: 1. Score your Final Scoring card(s) and all your cards with the end-of-game icon. Each Final Scoring card can grant up to 4 additional conservation points (by table or text, counting your universities, the cards in front of you, and their icons); you can never gain more than **4 conservation points from a single Final Scoring card**.
297: 2. Compute Victory Points: look at the scoring area where your Conservation counter is located and find the **lowest Appeal value in that scoring area** — this is your **Target Number**. **Victory Points = your Appeal value − your Target Number.**
298: 3. The player with the highest positive Victory Point total wins. **Tiebreaker:** the tied player who supported the most conservation projects wins (count the player tokens removed from the left side of the zoo map). If still tied, the tied players share the victory.
